newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end sharply down as institutions sell.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end sharply down as institutions sell.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed at a new three-year low on Thursday, dragged down sharply by heavy selling by institutions towards the close, brokers said.
The composite index was down 2.17 percent, or 15.30 points, to a provisional close of 689.38.
It was the lowest closing index since September 18, 1993, when the index closed at 685.94.

Brokers said institutions holding short positions on the index futures trading put a huge amount of sell orders to maximise their gains from futures trading as Thursday was the settlement date for December contracts.
"It was technical, and the impact was much stronger than we expected earlier," said Koh Soon-shik of LG Securities.
KOSPI-200 index, on which the futures contracts are being made, fell by 2.94 percent, or 2.12 points to 69.91.
Brokers said the overnight Wall Street plunge, which caused a nosedive in several Asian markets, had little immediate impact on the local market.
On Wednesday, the Dow lost 71 points or 1.09 percent to about 6,403 after falling nearly 130 points earlier.
The South Korean market was on a downward trend from mid-mornings when profit-taking emerged to take advantage of past two days of gains.
Brokers expected sharp falls to spark bargain hunting on Friday, although planned strikes led by the nation's largest labour union groups could affect the trading sentiment.
